about: The Phase 3 gate (docs/EVALS.md): 24 unattended tickets on an invoicing service with 5 CI policies found only by running CI, 2 environment quirks (CI in Asia/Kolkata; tests run in reverse order), a rule stated once in ticket 1 (integer cents, uuid4().hex ids), an early storage decision (ticket 4) that ticket 16 tests with 8 concurrent processes, a backup migration (ticket 12), a dependency temptation (ticket 18) and tickets that build on each other.
sessions: You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #1: products get a GST rate: `add_product(name, price_cents, tax_bp=1800)`, in basis points (1800 = 18 %). Add `invoice_total(invoice_id)` returning a dict with `subtotal_cents`, `tax_cents` and `total_cents`: each line's tax is its subtotal (quantity × unit price) times its product's rate, rounded half up to the cent, and the invoice's tax is the sum of its lines' tax. Two rules for this whole backlog, which later tickets won't repeat: money is always an integer number of cents, never a float; and every new kind of record gets its id from `uuid.uuid4().hex`. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #2: add `issue_invoice(invoice_id, due_days=30)`. A draft becomes `issued` and gets a `number` (`INV-0001`, `INV-0002`, … in the order invoices are issued; numbering starts again after `reset()`), `issued_at` (the current time from `invoicing.now()`, ISO-8601 UTC ending in `Z`) and `due_on` (the UTC date `due_days` days after it was issued, as `YYYY-MM-DD`); `get_invoice` shows all three. Issuing an invoice that isn't a draft raises ValueError. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #3: add `record_payment(invoice_id, amount_cents, method)` for issued invoices. It stores and returns a payment with `id`, `invoice_id`, `amount_cents`, `method` and `paid_at` (now, UTC ending in `Z`). The invoice's status becomes `partially_paid` after a payment and `paid` once its payments reach its total. Paying an invoice that isn't issued or partially paid, a non-positive amount, or more than is still owed raises ValueError. Also add `payments_for(invoice_id)`, oldest first. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #4: invoices must survive a restart. Add `open_store(path)`: from then on everything (customers, products, invoices, payments, and whatever later tickets add) lives in the file at `path`, and every change is saved by the time the call that made it returns, so another process that calls `open_store(path)` sees it. `open_store(None)` goes back to the in-memory store, and `reset()` empties whichever store is open. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #6: add `void_invoice(invoice_id, reason)`: an issued invoice with no payments becomes `void`, with `void_reason` and `voided_at` (now, UTC ending in `Z`) shown by `get_invoice`; anything else raises ValueError. A void invoice can't be paid and is never overdue. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #7: credit notes. Add `credit_note(invoice_id, amount_cents, reason)`: it records and returns a credit note (`id`, `invoice_id`, `amount_cents`, `reason`, `created_at`) against an issued or partially paid invoice. Add `balance_due(invoice_id)`: the total, less payments and credit notes. An invoice whose balance due reaches 0 is `paid`, and payments can't exceed the balance due. A non-positive credit, or one larger than the balance due, raises ValueError. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #8: add `customer_statement(customer_id, month)` for a month like `"2026-03"` (a UTC month). It returns `opening_cents` (what the customer owed before the month), `entries` and `closing_cents` (opening plus the month's invoices, less its payments and credit notes). `entries` lists, oldest first, each of the customer's invoices issued in the month (`{"type": "invoice", "id": <invoice id>, "at": <issued_at>, "amount_cents": <its total>}`), payments (`"payment"`, the payment's id, `paid_at`, amount) and credit notes (`"credit"`, the credit note's id, `created_at`, amount). Void invoices don't count. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #9: add `apply_discount(invoice_id, percent)` for drafts: a whole-number percentage from 0 to 100 taken off every line before tax. Each line's discount is its subtotal × percent / 100, rounded half up to the cent; tax is then charged on the discounted line, and `invoice_total`'s `subtotal_cents` is after the discount. A percentage outside 0 to 100, or an invoice that isn't a draft, raises ValueError. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #10: invoices in other currencies. `create_invoice(customer_id, lines, currency="INR")` takes a 3-letter currency code (`get_invoice` shows it); the invoice's amounts are cents of that currency, taking the catalogue's `price_cents` as its unit prices. Add `set_fx_rate(currency, rate)`, where `rate` is a string such as `"83.1250"` (INR per unit, up to 4 decimal places), and `total_in_inr(invoice_id)`: the invoice's total in INR cents, rounded half up. INR needs no rate; any other currency without one raises ValueError. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

It returns `{"count", "total_inr_cents", "average_inr_cents"}`: each payment is converted to INR at its invoice's currency's rate, rounded half up per payment, and the average is rounded half up to the cent (0 when there are no payments). Ticket #12: backups (`export_backup` / `import_backup`, format in the README) lose everything added since version 1: payments, credit notes, discounts, currencies, numbers, due dates, rates. Bump the backup format to version 2, which round-trips the whole store (numbering carries on after an import), and document it in the README. Version-1 files must still import: put the upgrade in `invoicing/migrations/v1_to_v2.py`. A version-1 invoice becomes an INR draft with no discount whose lines get the 18 % default rate. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #14: late fees. Add `apply_late_fees(today)` (`today` is a UTC `datetime.date`): every issued or partially paid invoice gets a late fee for each full 30 days it is past `due_on` (one at 30 days, another at 60, …), never twice for the same period. Each fee is 1.5 % of the balance due at the moment it's added, rounded half up, and fees are added one period at a time. Fees aren't taxed; they add to `balance_due` and to `invoice_total`, which reports them as `late_fees_cents` (included in `total_cents`). It returns the fees it added, oldest `due_on` first, as `[{"invoice_id", "cents"}]`. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the invoicing service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #15: recurring invoices. Add `create_schedule(customer_id, lines, every_days, start)` (`lines` as for `create_invoice`, `start` a `datetime.date`), returning the schedule with its `id`, and `run_schedules(today)`: for each occurrence (`start`, `start + every_days`, …) up to and including `today` that hasn't been invoiced yet, it creates the invoice and issues it (due in 30 days). It returns the new invoices (as `get_invoice` shows them), oldest occurrence first. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

No payment may be lost or counted twice, and statuses and balances must stay right. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #17: add `refund_payment(payment_id, amount_cents, reason)`: it records and returns a refund (`id`, `payment_id`, `amount_cents`, `reason`, `created_at`). A refund reduces what the payment counts for, so `balance_due` goes back up, and a `paid` invoice becomes `partially_paid`. A non-positive refund, or more than is left of the payment after earlier refunds, raises ValueError. Also add `refunds_for(invoice_id)`, oldest first. Strings are double-quoted, numbers are bare, and a draft's number is `null`. Export what you add from the `invoicing` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.
